correctness.rationale: For every equiangular pentagon, projection of midpoint-difference vectors gives \(\Delta_i\ge g_i\). The closure equation converts the weighted four-gap sum into a strictly positive combination of all five side lengths. For every omitted pair, another pair is separated by at least \(qL/12\); thus at least two are. An explicit positive-length closure example has exactly three additional intersections by exact radical comparisons. The standalone checker reproduces all symbolic identities and verifies the nine-edge unrestricted contrast using integer inequalities. The proof does not rely on random numerical tests.

originality.rationale: The earlier planar side-disk theorem establishes at least one disjoint pair in a convex pentagon, equivalently at most nine graph edges, and the later treewidth-three theorem does not forbid the nine-edge graph. value.rationale: The geometry of side-diameter disks in convex pentagons motivated the foundational planarity problem. Equiangular pentagons form the simplest nonregular odd fixed-angle family, and a uniform two-nonedge guarantee plus sharp eight-edge maximum is a substantive stability and extremal refinement, not a renaming or a new parameter in an existing formula. The explicit proportional separation is robust under perturbation; the unrestricted nine-edge witness shows the restriction has geometric content.
